title: Fluorescent pulse-chase labeling to monitor mitochondrial degradation in neurons
author: Schneider, Evans

steps.title: Prepare media and sterilize tools
steps.instruction: Prepare AM and Maintenance Media (MM) for primary hippocampal cultures, pre‑warm 5 mL HBSS and 35 mL AM at 37 °C, place 10 mL HBSS in a 15 mL conical tube on ice, and sterilize scissors, forceps and the dissection area with 70 % ethanol.

substeps.instruction: Prepare AM and MM for primary hippocampal cultures.
Pre‑warm 5 mL HBSS and 35 mL AM in a 37 °C water bath.
Place 10 mL HBSS in a 15 mL conical tube on ice.
Sterilize scissors, forceps, and the dissection area with 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Transiently transfect neurons
steps.instruction: At 6 DIV, verify neuronal health, save each dish’s media, replace with fresh equilibrated MM, then prepare DNA‑Lipofectamine complexes and add them to the cultures as described.

substeps.instruction: At 6 DIV, inspect each imaging dish for viable neurons.
For each dish, remove the existing media, save it for later use, and replace with fresh equilibrated MM.
In a sterile 1.5 mL tube (Tube 1), mix 150 µL Neurobasal medium with DNA: 0.35 µg Mito‑SNAP, 0.4 µg Halo‑OPTN, and 0.4 µg LAMP1‑EGFP.
In a second sterile tube (Tube 2), mix 150 µL Neurobasal medium with 4 µL Lipofectamine 2000.
Incubate both tubes at room temperature (20‑22 °C) for 5 min.
Add the contents of Tube 2 to Tube 1, gently pipette‑mix, and incubate at 20‑22 °C for 20 min to form DNA‑Lipofectamine complexes.
Add the transfection complexes dropwise to the neuron cultures and incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 45 min.
During the 45‑min incubation, add an equal volume of the saved media (from step 2) mixed with fresh MM that has been equilibrated at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
After 45 min, replace the neurons’ media with the conditioned media prepared in the previous substep.
Note: complete the transfection ~18 h before starting the pulse‑chase labeling.

steps.title: Perform pulse‑chase labeling
steps.instruction: The day after transfection, induce mitochondrial damage for 6 h, apply the first SNAP pulse to label “Old” mitochondria, add a non‑fluorescent SNAP Block for 2 h, incubate ~16 h, then apply a second SNAP pulse to label “Young” mitochondria before imaging.

substeps.instruction: Induce mitochondrial damage (e.g., antioxidant deprivation) for 6 h.
Label damaged mitochondria with the first SNAP pulse (magenta, “Old” Mito‑SNAP).
Add a non‑fluorescent SNAP Block and incubate for 2 h to saturate remaining SNAP sites.
Leave the neurons untreated for approximately 16 h.
Perform a second SNAP pulse (green, “Young” Mito‑SNAP) immediately before imaging.

steps.title: Analyze images in Fiji
steps.instruction: Open the acquired image stacks in Fiji, assign channels, identify OPTN‑positive “Old” mitochondria, assess LAMP1 colocalization, quantify event ratios, generate line scans, subtract background, normalize intensities, and prepare graphical summaries.

substeps.instruction: Open image files in Fiji and assign channels: 1 = Young Mito‑SNAP (SNAP‑Cell 430), 2 = Old Mito‑SNAP (SNAP JF549cp), 3 = LAMP1‑EGFP, 4 = Halo‑OPTN (JF646x).
Use the Channels Tool to visualize channels and manually scroll through the Z‑stack to locate Halo‑OPTN rings.
For each Halo‑OPTN ring, determine labeling: (i) dual‑labeled with Young and Old SNAP signals, or (ii) only Old SNAP signal.
Draw a Rectangle around each clear OPTN‑positive “Old” event (only Old SNAP signal).
Using the same rectangles, assess LAMP1‑EGFP colocalization: score events as LAMP1‑positive (overlapping rings) or LAMP1‑negative (no overlap).
Count LAMP1‑positive and LAMP1‑negative events; calculate ratios: LAMP1‑positive / total OPTN‑positive Old events and LAMP1‑negative / total.
For representative events, draw a 1‑pixel‑wide Line through the Halo‑OPTN ring.
For each channel, select Plot Profile → List to obtain fluorescence intensity values along the line.
Measure background intensity by drawing a Rectangle in an area without signal, using Analyze → Measure; repeat in multiple areas and compute the average background for each channel.
Subtract the average background intensity from the line‑scan values for each channel.
Normalize each channel’s corrected intensities by dividing every value by the highest intensity value observed in that channel (setting the maximum to 1).
Create bar graphs, scatter plots, or pie charts to present the ratios and include representative images.
